children.name: Resection Planning and Margins
children.blurb: This page covers AI systems that help surgical teams plan tissue resection and define safe margins before and during an operation.

children.name: Haptic Feedback in Robotic Surgery
children.blurb: Haptic feedback in robotic surgery covers the sensing, transmission, and display of force, vibration, and tissue compliance information between a surgical robot's instruments and the surgeon at a console.

children.name: Virtual Surgical Rehearsal
children.blurb: Virtual surgical rehearsal uses patient-specific imaging and computational models to let a surgical team practice a planned procedure before entering the operating room.

children.name: Tremor Stabilisation in Microsurgery
children.blurb: Tremor stabilisation in microsurgery covers technologies that reduce or cancel physiological hand tremor during delicate procedures such as retinal, vascular, and neurosurgery.

children.name: Remote Telesurgery
children.blurb: Remote telesurgery is the practice of performing surgical procedures on a patient from a distance using robotic instruments, telecommunication links, and real-time imaging.

sections.body: Surgical robotics and navigation covers AI systems that help plan, guide, and perform operations. In practice, AI is used to outline tumor margins from scans before cutting, to steady a surgeon's hand during fine work, and to let a surgeon rehearse a specific patient's anatomy in simulation. Some systems also relay force sensations back through robotic instruments, and a few experimental setups allow an operator to control a robot from another location. These are working tools in operating rooms and research labs, not just proposals.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field is uneven. Resection planning and tremor reduction are the most mature, with cleared devices in regular use for orthopedics, neurosurgery, and some soft tissue work. Haptic feedback remains limited because reproducing realistic touch through a console is hard, and most commercial robots give only partial or simplified force cues. Virtual rehearsal is useful for anatomy but still cannot predict how living tissue will bleed, swell, or tear. Remote telesurgery works over short, fast, private links, but distance, latency, and network reliability still cap how far and how safely it can go. The honest limit is that no current system replaces a surgeon's judgment, and every step still needs human oversight.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader looking at how AI decides where to cut should start with Resection Planning and Margins, which explains tumor boundary mapping and safe tissue removal. Haptic Feedback in Robotic Surgery covers the sense of touch in a machine, and pairs naturally with Tremor Stabilisation in Microsurgery, where fine motor control and force sensing meet. Virtual Surgical Rehearsal shows how patient specific models are built and practiced on before the real operation. Remote Telesurgery sits at the far end of the chain, asking what happens when the surgeon is not in the room, and it depends on the planning, feedback, and stability covered in the other pages.
